# Template: water_cycle
A landscape cross-section of the hydrological cycle: sun in the top-left corner, ocean on the left, a mountain on the right, clouds overhead, rain or snow falling on the mountain, a river running back to the sea, and a groundwater aquifer under the surface, with curved arrows for evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration (plus optional transpiration from trees). Choose this scene for any request about the water cycle or hydrological cycle, evaporation and condensation, precipitation, 'where does rain come from', runoff and infiltration, or groundwater recharge. Stages can be shown selectively so the narration can build the cycle one step at a time.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "stages": {
   "type": "array",
   "items": {
    "type": "string",
    "enum": [
     "evaporation",
     "condensation",
     "precipitation",
     "runoff",
     "infiltration",
     "transpiration"
    ]
   },
   "description": "Which cycle stages to draw arrows (and labels) for. Default: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration. Use a subset to build the cycle up step by step."
  },
  "transpiration": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show trees on the land with dashed transpiration arrows rising to the cloud (default false). Equivalent to adding 'transpiration' to stages."
  },
  "groundwater": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show the water table, the shaded aquifer, bedrock hatching and the groundwater flow arrow toward the sea (default true)."
  },
  "labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Show stage name labels (default true). Set false when the narration will name each stage instead."
  },
  "precipType": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "rain",
    "snow",
    "both"
   ],
   "description": "Falling precipitation on the mountain: slanted rain dashes, snowflakes, or snow high up with rain lower down (default 'rain')."
  },
  "labelText": {
   "type": "object",
   "description": "Override the text of individual labels (e.g. translations or simpler wording).",
   "properties": {
    "evaporation": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "condensation": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "precipitation": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "runoff": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "infiltration": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "transpiration": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "ocean": {
     "type": "string"
    },
    "groundwater": {
     "type": "string"
    }
   }
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- sun / sun_rays: the sun disc in the top-left corner and its rays
- ocean_fill / ocean_surface: the sea on the left and its wavy surface line
- land_fill / land_surface: the land cross-section and the seabed-to-mountain profile
- trees: small trees on the lower slope (transpiration only)
- river: the river running down the slope back to the sea
- aquifer_fill / water_table / bedrock / bedrock_hatch: the groundwater zone, its dashed water table, and the impermeable bedrock
- cloud_small / cloud_small_fill / cloud_main / cloud_main_fill: the forming cloud over the sea and the big rain cloud over the mountain
- evaporation: curved arrows rising from the ocean surface
- transpiration: dashed arrows rising from the trees
- condensation: the arrow feeding vapour from the small cloud into the rain cloud
- rain / snow: the falling precipitation strokes on the mountain
- runoff: arrows of surface flow down the slope
- infiltration: arrows soaking down from the surface to the water table
- gw_flow: the dashed groundwater flow arrow back to the sea
- label_evaporation / label_condensation / label_precipitation / label_runoff / label_infiltration / label_transpiration / label_ocean / label_groundwater: the stage name labels
Examples:
Request: "Draw the water cycle." → params: {}
Request: "Explain evaporation and transpiration only — no groundwater, snow on the peak." → params: {"stages":["evaporation","condensation"],"transpiration":true,"groundwater":false,"precipType":"snow"}

In YAML: `template: water_cycle` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
